title: Roundtables: Inside the Quest for Cognitive Immortality
gist: Promotional listing for a subscriber-only MIT Technology Review Roundtables event on November 17, 2026, in which Mary Beth Griggs and Antonio Regalado discuss technologies aimed at extending the mind beyond death, such as gradual brain replacement and uploading memories to the cloud. Related links note drugmaker claims that GLP-1 weight-loss drugs reduce molecular markers of aging.

insights.claim: Some technologists are pursuing ways to keep a person's mind going even beyond death, including gradual brain replacement and uploading memories to the cloud, which MIT Technology Review will cover in a subscriber-only event on November 17, 2026.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Signals a fringe but growing longevity/neurotech niche drawing mainstream tech-press attention.

insights.claim: MIT Technology Review's related coverage reports a stealthy startup that pitched brainless human clones and technology that lets people 'speak' to dead relatives, indicating active commercial experimentation around digital and biological continuity of the self.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Early-stage 'grief tech' and radical-longevity ventures carry high ethical and regulatory risk.

insights.claim: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly report that their GLP-1 weight-loss drugs reduce molecular markers of biological aging, while separate studies cast doubt on young-organ transplants as a rejuvenation route.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Anti-aging claims could expand the addressable narrative for GLP-1 franchises, though evidence here is only a headline-level mention.
insights.locator: Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing
